candidates.excerpt: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released PostgreSQL 19, introducing changes to database maintenance, query planning, replication, and application development. The release focuses on reducing administrative overhead and improving performance, with new tools for reorganizing tables without downtime and controlling query plans. By Robert Krzaczyński

candidates.title: Claude Code Has Been Leaking Secrets Through Its "Don't Ask Again" Feature
candidates.excerpt: Agentic security firm Apiiro found that Claude Code has been exposing secrets in public repositories due to how it stores them in local file on developers' machines to implement "Don't Ask Again". The company identified 1,122 secrets in claude/settings.local.json files and another 1,160 in git history, in the shared settings.json, and in agent chat transcripts stored in repos. By Sergio De Simone

candidates.title: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
candidates.excerpt: Google recently announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service that runs AI agents in isolated microVMs, with checkpointing capabilities to suspend and resume execution environments. The design keeps credentials, API keys, and OAuth refresh tokens outside the agent sandbox, using an external Agent Gateway to authenticate requests and inject the required secrets. By Renato Losio

candidates.title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
candidates.excerpt: AWS Lambda now runs Event Functions on EC2 G-series GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU, vLLM and SGLang base images that need no handler code, and 90-minute asynchronous timeouts. Billing is the instance price plus a 9.75 percent fee; first hands-on tests report an eight-minute publish and no response streaming. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

candidates.excerpt: By Leo Babauta Something I’ve noticed is that a lot of us have an ingrained belief that we can take some time off to rest if we’ve worked hard enough. Or often it’s like, “I’ll rest now so I can be more productive tomorrow.” The mindset we have ingrained in us is that rest has to be justified by how productive it will help us to be . This is so deeply ingrained in us that we don’t even notice it. It comes from the mindset that we need to be more productive, and that our lives have to be built…

candidates.title: The Joy of Falling Behind
candidates.excerpt: By Leo Babauta A lot of people right now are feeling like they just can’t keep up with everything — it’s just too much. And it feels like the pace of everything we have to keep up with is accelerating. There’s more and more, and it’s coming at us faster and faster.
